items.evidence: "The project covers a television remote control... The design should be original, trendy, and user-friendly."

Notes list the four roles ("The project manager, marketing expert, user-interface designer, and industrial designer kicked off...") but omit what each one covers (user needs, usability, engineering/materials).
"The work will proceed in three design phases. The first phase is functional design." Transcript says three phases, matching the notes.
Notes mention the project folder for materials and minutes, but not the PM's walkthrough of the SMARTboard (pen, eraser, colour, line width, slides).
"The target selling price is €25, with production costing approximately €12.50."
Section "Whiteboard sketches" covers all four drawing animals: dolphin, elephant, tiger, ant.
"added intuitive controls, accessibility, and lightweight materials to the design considerations."
Answer key has no action items; the notes' one action item is listed under errors.
"The assignment is for a TV remote, not a multi-device remote."
"The interface designer urged familiarity... Mark summarized the aim as an intuitive design." (the 'rational changes' wording is garbled; see errors)
"Mark said the product should reach almost everyone and agreed accessibility should be considered."
"Xavier said the remote should be made of lightweight material." PM replied "It should be light, okay."

errors.claim: The interface designer urged familiarity and rational changes.
errors.why_wrong: Transcript: "No rational changes or whatever, 'cause it revolutionary changes" - he meant avoiding radical/revolutionary changes, not urging changes.

errors.claim: Share the marketing ideas at the follow-up (owner: Dirk Mengveld)
errors.why_wrong: Dirk only said he had some ideas and trailed off; no task to present them at the next meeting was agreed. Answer key lists no action items.
